summary: Built as a steel tower on the J. Clark Salyer refuge, moved to the Turtle Mountains in 1957; the register says a radio relay now, firelookout.org says removed.

facts.status_note: The NHLR entry says the tower is now primarily a radio relay station. The firelookout.org list marks the Turtle Mountain tower as removed. The sources disagree, and no source read settles it.

events.note: Transferred from the U.S. Fish & Wildlife Service refuge to the North Dakota Forest Service; then reconstructed in the Turtle Mountains for fire detection
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, July 1, 1991

corrections.proposed: disputed: NHLR says standing and in use as a radio relay station; firelookout.org says removed
corrections.why: The brief's gone status matches firelookout.org, but the NHLR entry describes the steel tower as still in use. The sources disagree and no source read settles it, so the status is flagged rather than changed to standing.

sources.title: Turtle Mountain Tower (US 20, ND 1), National Historic Lookout Register

notes_for_editor: The register and the firelookout.org list conflict on whether the steel tower still stands; the register's 'now primarily used as a radio relay station' is the only current-status claim found, and the register's own entry is undated. The register also calls it 'the only fire lookout in North Dakota', but its state page now lists a second one, Rugby Tower (was Salyer Wildlife Refuge Tower, US 1414, added 2020), which was not used in the story. No build year, staffing dates, or public-access information was found, so none is given. The brief's note that NHLR lists lookouts standing when registered is not resolved by these sources. The brief's status 'gone' should be checked by a person before the record changes; no physical check was made.
